doc.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

title: First chart written for a Bronx kids' band
summary: His first arrangement, a Pepsi Cola jingle chart for a teenage Bronx band with Shorty Rogers, Eddie Bert, Lenny Hambro and Stan Getz.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Can you recall the first thing that you wrote for somebody, and hearing it back?

Yeah. We had a band up in the Bronx. I didn’t live in the Bronx but I used to go to the Bronx to play with these kids and we were high school people, I think I was 16 or 17. In the band was Shorty Rodgers, let me see, the trombone player DeVito, Eddie Bert, a whole bunch of all young kids in the band. Lenny Hambro, who wound up playing with Gene Krupa for years and years, a great alto player. And we were all kids. And somehow or other I wrote a chart on the Pepsi Cola jingle. “Pepsi Cola hits the spot.” And every

time I used to run into Shorty Rodgers, 50 years later, he wound sing the end of the bridge [scats], which is very strange. That was our greeting. He’d look at me and go [scats]. Memory. I think memory has a lot to do with musicality. I can remember things that I heard in those days, I can remember things I heard yesterday too, but I mean I’ll go back to solos that I played and still remember them, little parts of charts that really hit me. Oh also in the band was Stan Getz as a youngster, a lot of very good players from that area.
